title: Drummer change: JJ Joyce replaces Bob McIntyre
summary: JJ Joyce, a dental student with a parade-style snare and bass drum approach, replaced Bob McIntyre; otherwise the band is unchanged.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I want to get the band, as it's changed now. Have you had any substitute drummers in since JJ started?

Well, the original drummer with the group was Bob McIntyre. And, well, a couple months back, Bob's wife had a baby. And, naturally, Bob had to give more time to his family, you know, and he couldn't get out the way he wanted to make these jobs at night. And, then, John Joyce, JJ started playing with us. And, from what I hear, I don't know, it might just be a rumor. But, JJ Joyce has won the Trap Drumming Championship at Mississippi State for about four years in a row. Now, I don't know how authentic that is, but he is very good. He's a very good drummer. He's a young boy, I mean, he, but he, uh, he just happened to catch that old New Orleans style of drumming, you know. He's not a cymbal player. He's just a sophomore, isn't he? I think so. He's a, he's a dental student. I might get him to make a bridge for me, you know. I need teeth something awful right now. And, uh, a trumpet player without teeth is like a barber without hands, you know.
It's more like bunk, huh? They bought bunk teeth, maybe they'll buy me some teeth. Well, I might get lucky one day.
Uh, let's see now. Have you had any changes? Your trombone player didn't go to Europe with you. No. You had the same trombone player all along, you had the same clarinet player, except he didn't go.
Let's see, who else might have changed? I don't think anybody has.

Well, no, it's, uh, it's been pretty much the same, same group, you know. Uh, maybe one, uh, one fellow might sit in for another one Sunday, you know. But we keep pretty much around the same bunch of guys that had been playing, you know.
But you don't have cymbal drummers, huh?

No, he, uh, he beats a real, well, I think this boy could get by on just a snare drum and a bass drum alone. Uh, I mean, it has more of that parade sound. In a parade, you didn't have all these, uh, all these cymbals and all the wood chocks and whatnot. And, uh, of course he does know how to play them, but, uh, in this particular style of music we play, uh, he relies mostly on his snare and bass drum.
